evidence: j1.stderr: `node product/cli.js greet` printed 'no greeting' on stderr, with empty stdout (j1.stdout, 0 bytes) and exit 1
j1-diagnosis.txt: same result on repeat runs and after re-running product/setup.js (exit 0)
journeys.note: The first step of the 2-step budget failed in about 0.02 s, well inside the 60 s budget, and no greeting was produced. This is not a bring-up failure: setup had already run (out/setup.done was present), and re-running it did not help because it never creates the greeting file.

evidence: j2.stderr: `node product/cli.js` printed 'usage: cli.js ping <url> | greet'
j1-diagnosis.txt: the no-argument run exits 2 with the same usage line on repeat
journeys.note: With no arguments the CLI names its two subcommands and exits non-zero, so the user learns how to use it. The usage line goes to stderr and is terse, but it is enough for this journey. Following its `greet` suggestion leads into the J-1 failure, which is reported under J-1.

evidence: j1.stdout is empty and j1.stderr contains 'no greeting' for `node product/cli.js greet`, exit 1
j1-diagnosis.txt: after `node product/setup.js` (exit 0), `greet` still prints 'no greeting' and exits 1; product/ contains no greeting.txt
j1-diagnosis.txt: `git grep greeting` finds only readers (product/cli.js:4, product/server.js:6-7); `git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'product/greeting*'` returns nothing
j1-diagnosis.txt: with a temporary product/greeting.txt containing 'hello', `greet` printed 'hello' and exited 0; removing the file brought the failure back, and git status is clean
findings.claim: Asking the greeter CLI for a greeting always fails on a fresh, set-up checkout: it prints 'no greeting', exits 1 and gives no greeting. J-1 cannot be completed.
findings.cause: The CLI reads product/greeting.txt, but nothing in the product supplies that file. It is not tracked, was never committed on any ref, and product/setup.js only writes out/setup.done. The reader works when the file exists, so the defect is the missing greeting content or provisioning, not the read logic or the environment.

evidence: j1.stderr: the whole error text is 'no greeting', with no file path and no remedy
findings.claim: The greet error does not tell the user how to fix the problem and only vaguely says what failed. The design requires an error to name what failed and how to fix it, but 'no greeting' does not name the missing product/greeting.txt or give any remedy, so the user is stuck.
findings.cause: The missing-file branch in product/cli.js writes a fixed bare message, with no file path or corrective step.

premises.claim: The CLI greet command depends on product/greeting.txt and fails with the bare message 'no greeting' when it is absent.
Product setup writes only out/setup.done and does not create a greeting file.
The design reference requires an error to name what failed and how to fix it.
With no arguments the CLI prints a usage line naming ping and greet and exits 2.

reasons: J-1 is blocked by a product defect: greet fails on every run, including after setup, because the product never supplies its greeting. MS-1's CLI promise is therefore not met.
J-2 completed: the no-argument usage line is adequate.
The bare 'no greeting' message is reported separately as a design deviation, because it would still need fixing if the greeting file were provisioned and the message remained reachable.

Not exercised: the web half of MS-1. No web journey is declared and the product block declares no ports, so I did not start product/server.js. This walk gives no runtime verdict on the web path. From source only, product/server.js:6 reads the same missing file, but that is unconfirmed at runtime and is not reported as a finding.
The temporary product/greeting.txt was a diagnostic in my detached checkout and was removed afterwards. Re-running setup only rewrote the git-ignored out/setup.done. git status was clean at the end.
